properties.description: January 15, 1929 — Martin Luther King Jr. is born in Atlanta, Georgia.

properties.event: Becomes pastor at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church
properties.description: Installed in 1954 at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, Montgomery, Alabama — King’s first full-time pastorship and base for early organizing.
December 5, 1955 — Following Rosa Parks’s arrest, the Montgomery Bus Boycott launches; King becomes president of the MIA.
December 20, 1956 — After 381–382 days, boycott ends as the Supreme Court’s Browder v. Gayle ruling desegregates Montgomery buses.
January 10, 1957 — Southern Christian Leadership Conference is founded in Atlanta, with King as a leading figure for nonviolent direct action.
April 16, 1963 — While jailed in Birmingham, Alabama, King pens his famous letter defending nonviolent resistance to unjust laws.
August 28, 1963 — At the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers the "I Have a Dream" speech to ~250,000 people.
July 2, 1964 — President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act in Washington, D.C., landmark legislation long championed by King and the movement.
December 10, 1964 — King receives the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo, Norway, at age 35.
March 7, 1965 — Peaceful voting-rights marchers are brutally attacked on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, galvanizing national support.
March 25, 1965 — King delivers "How Long? Not Long!" at the Alabama State Capitol after the successful five-day march for voting rights.
August 6, 1965 — President Johnson signs the Voting Rights Act at the U.S. Capitol, banning discriminatory voting practices.
1966 — King and SCLC campaign in Chicago for open housing and economic justice; marches highlight segregation in the North.
April 4, 1967 — At Riverside Church in New York City, King publicly opposes the Vietnam War and links militarism, racism, and poverty.
April 3, 1968 — In Memphis, Tennessee, King delivers “I’ve Been to the Mountaintop,” supporting striking sanitation workers.
April 4, 1968 — King is assassinated at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee.
